note: Seeded departures from the US Federal Plain Language Guidelines the plain brief names: "shall" for a requirement, legalese, sentences over 45 words, undefined abbreviations, needless passive voice, abstract nouns, third-person "applicants" or "employees" instead of "you", a dense paragraph that should be a list, and a main point buried at the end. The rest of each document already addresses the reader as "you" in short sentences.

parking-permit-notice.md.quote: at three public meetings last year the council heard from many residents
parking-permit-notice.md.issue: A 52-word sentence; split it into two or three short ones.

parking-permit-notice.md.quote: The zone will be managed by the Department of Transportation and Mobility.
parking-permit-notice.md.issue: Passive voice; "The Department of Transportation and Mobility will manage the zone."

parking-permit-notice.md.quote: you shall live at an address
Applicants are advised that each permit is tied to a single vehicle
parking-permit-notice.md.issue: Speaks about "applicants" in the third person (and in the passive); address the reader as "you".

parking-permit-notice.md.quote: To apply, complete the online form at ashgrove.example/parking.
parking-permit-notice.md.issue: A dense paragraph packs the steps, documents, fee and timing together; break it into a numbered list.

parking-permit-notice.md.quote: Most important of all: enforcement starts on 1 April.
parking-permit-notice.md.issue: The main point (residents need a permit from 1 April and must apply by 1 March) is buried at the end under "Other information"; put it first.

travel-expense-memo.md.quote: Mileage reimbursement for the utilization of a personal vehicle will be effectuated at the rate of 70 cents per mile.
travel-expense-memo.md.issue: Abstract nouns and legalese ("utilization", "effectuated"); "If you drive your own car, we pay you 70 cents a mile."

travel-expense-memo.md.quote: Employees traveling overnight must book lodging
travel-expense-memo.md.issue: Speaks about "employees" in the third person; address the reader as "you" ("If you stay overnight, book your hotel...").

travel-expense-memo.md.quote: You need a receipt for every expense over $25.
travel-expense-memo.md.issue: A dense paragraph of six separate receipt rules; break it into a list.

travel-expense-memo.md.quote: attach the cancellation notice together with a short note from your manager
travel-expense-memo.md.issue: The cancelled-trips paragraph is one 57-word sentence; split it into short sentences or steps.

travel-expense-memo.md.quote: Payments will be made by the Finance Office within ten business days of approval
travel-expense-memo.md.issue: Passive voice; "We will pay you within ten business days of approval."

tax-assessment-letter.md.quote: the results for the subject property are set forth herein
tax-assessment-letter.md.issue: Legalese ("subject property", "set forth herein"); "here are the results for your home".

tax-assessment-letter.md.quote: Home values in Owensford rose steadily over the last four years
tax-assessment-letter.md.issue: A 53-word sentence; split it into short ones.

tax-assessment-letter.md.quote: The property owner may request an informal review
tax-assessment-letter.md.issue: Speaks about "the property owner" in the third person; address the reader as "you".

tax-assessment-letter.md.quote: you shall file a formal appeal
may be claimed on Form PX-2, which can be obtained at our office or downloaded from our website
tax-assessment-letter.md.issue: Passive voice; "You can claim these exemptions on Form PX-2, which you can get at our office or download from our website."

tax-assessment-letter.md.quote: the assessed value of your home has gone up from $312,000 to $368,000
tax-assessment-letter.md.issue: The main point of the letter, the new assessed value, is buried in the last paragraph under "Other information"; put it first.
